narrative:
Based on your application, the model estimated a 59% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning more than half of similar applicants would default. That high likelihood led to the denial.

Three key factors stood out. The strongest concern was your checking account balance, which was only between 0 and 200 DM. Among customers who are approved, most have no checking account at all or a much higher balance, so a low balance like yours signals limited financial cushion and was the biggest push toward a bad-risk rating.

The second factor was another installment plan you have at a bank. This was concerning because it suggests an additional monthly obligation, leaving less room to repay a new loan. Very few approved applicants have bank installment plans, so this significantly increased the risk.

Curiously, your credit history, which was marked as critical or with other credits, actually pushed the model slightly in the opposite direction—toward good credit. While that history might sound negative, in combination with your other details, it did not weigh as heavily as the checking balance and existing installment plan. It slightly offset, not outweighed, the other risks.

To improve your chances next time, focus on building a stronger checking account balance and paying off or closing your other bank installment plan. You may also want to wait until your credit history shows more completed payments. Reapplying after these changes would give you a far better outcome.
